key_insight: PD-CogT-Sleep will test whether deep-sleep enhancement using phase-targeted auditory stimulation improves cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment.
clinical_relevance: If effective, this non-pharmacological combination could strengthen cognitive training benefits, but cognitive and disease-modifying effects remain unproven.
method: Single-center, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial targeting 50 participants.
Participants randomized 1:1 to digital cognitive training plus auditory stimulation or cognitive training plus sham.
Assessments at baseline, five weeks post-allocation, and three-month follow-up.
evidence_signal: This design paper reports no efficacy results; planned evaluation prioritizes executive function, with additional cognitive, participant-reported, blood biomarker, and sleep EEG outcomes.
watch_item: The small, single-center trial may limit generalizability, and exploratory biomarker changes would not establish slowed disease progression.
paper_title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
